operand_normalization_rules.name: whitespace_and_case
operand_normalization_rules.reason: llvm-objdump inserts spaces inside Neon register lists (e.g. '{ v0.h }[1]') and differs in letter casing for hex digits or system operand identifiers; whitespace between tokens and ASCII letter case do not change operand meaning.

operand_normalization_rules.name: numeric_value
operand_normalization_rules.reason: llvm-objdump mixes hexadecimal and decimal immediates (hex for general/address immediates, decimal for shifts/bitfields, both in hints, 16-zero '#0000000000000000' for movi.2d #0, 8-decimal-place floats like '#1.00000000'), whereas MachGraph uses decimal below 16, hex at 16+, and '%.6g' for floats. Signed integers (hex or decimal) and floating-point literals are compared by exact mathematical value; the '#' immediate prefix is not part of the numeric value and must match on both sides.

operand_normalization_rules.name: adrp_comment_address
operand_normalization_rules.reason: Under --macho, llvm-objdump prints a signed page count as adrp's immediate operand and places the resolved target page address in the trailing '; 0x...' comment, whereas MachGraph prints the resolved page address directly.

operand_normalization_rules.name: pc_relative_offset
operand_normalization_rules.reason: llvm-objdump prints PC-relative '#offset' for adr and unbracketed literal loads (ldr, ldrsw, prfm), whereas MachGraph prints the resolved target address (instruction PC + offset).
